$comment: Machine-readable migration state, one entry per domain area. Read by tests/parity/ownership-guard.mjs and, from session 2 onward, by site/erp-bridge.js. Update this file in the SAME commit that changes an area's owner — never lag behind the code.

owner.engine: Fully implemented in site/erp-engine.js today; erp.html reads/writes it directly or via ErpBridge pass-through.
owner.factory: Implemented as a packages/ capability, reached through site/erp-bridge.js. erp-engine.js may still hold a shrinking legacy copy during transition; erp.html must not call it directly once an area is 'factory'.
owner.unbuilt: No implementation anywhere yet (neither erp-engine.js nor packages/). Net-new capability work.

$schema.specSection: Section number in Requirements/20260731_REQUERMIENTOS BÁSICO CANEI.docx this area corresponds to.
$schema.engineSection: The section-divider comment in site/erp-engine.js that implements this area today, or null if unbuilt.
$schema.plannedSession: The session number (see the plan) expected to move this area to its next owner state.

scheduling-gantt.note: Owned end to end by @repo/capability-scheduling and reached only through site/erp-bridge.js (ErpBridge.scheduling.plans). Session 5 built the domain — working calendar, FS/SS/FF dependencies with lead/lag, CPM with float and critical path, append-only baselines — and session 6 built the chart in erp.html (Proyectos → Seguimiento técnico) that consumes it: drag to move, edge-drag to resize, knob-drag to link, freeze and compare a baseline. The view computes no dates: every date, float, critical flag and drift on screen came from the capability. Plans persist in state.plans (schema v3), which the engine serialises without knowing what it is. engineSection is null because erp-engine.js never implemented this area.

extraction-ocr.note: Session 7 built the reading half: @repo/capability-extraction turns recognised text into candidate fields with confidence, provenance and arithmetic checks, and @repo/pack-jurisdiction-es-es supplies the profile behind the extraction-profile@1 port (number and date notation, NIF/CIF/NIE and IBAN check characters, the words each field is announced by, the rates in force on a date). Still 'unbuilt' here because no screen reaches it: session 8 adds the camera, the recognition adapter and the validation screen, and flips this. Nothing is ever auto-confirmed — CAP-04 is enforced by the capability's type, which always reports confirmed:false.

three-panel-shell.note: Built in session 4, but purely in the view layer of site/erp.html — sections, subsections, the global bar and hash routing. engineSection is null because there is no business rule here to own: the shell reads counts and alerts through the same engine calls the views already use. Recorded as 'engine' rather than 'unbuilt' because it exists and is in use; there is no owner value for 'view-only'.

task-status-summary.note: First area served by the capability layer. Task counts by status are computed by @repo/capability-scheduling via site/erp-bridge.js, not by ad-hoc filtering in the view. The underlying task records are still owned by erp-engine.js (see alerts-tasks-control-tower) — only this derivation moved, which is what made it safe to land first.
